text: dsh-code-impact 是一个面向 DSH Web 客户端的代码理解插件。它在 agent 会话中注册 code_query 和 code_verify：前者从工作区索引查询符号定义、文件声明、引用位置、继承关系和索引状态，后者在编辑后重新索引改动文件并归纳接口变化、实现变化和失效引用。插件还在设置页提供工作区索引浏览界面，可查看架构、导入关系、类型继承与调用记录，并为指定目录建立索引。适合希望快速定位代码关系、检查修改影响并浏览项目结构的 DSH 用户。无需 API key；索引和调用记录缓存在 DSH 配置目录中。

dsh-code-impact indexes DSH workspaces for code navigation. code_query finds symbols, references, file outlines, and inheritance; code_verify summarizes edits and dangling references. A page shows architecture and imports. No API key is needed; index and call records are cached locally.
我想查一个函数在哪定义、哪些地方引用了它。
改完代码后，帮我看哪些调用点可能需要跟着调整。
Show me the inheritance tree and members for a type in my workspace.
dsh-code-impact 的功能「代码关系查询」：agent 调用 code_query，按符号名或文件查询定义、引用、继承和索引状态，并返回带文件位置的结果。
dsh-code-impact 的功能「编辑影响核对」：agent 编辑后调用 code_verify，插件重新索引变化文件并汇总接口变化、仅实现变化及失效引用。

dsh-code-impact README · dsh-code-impact：**Post-edit impact checks for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) — a symbol index, a reference graph, and an inheritance model that answer "what did this edit touch?" instead of "grep the repo and re-run everything".**

dsh-code-impact README · Why：Every small edit — a default value, a rename, a deleted method — triggers the same ceremony:
search the whole repo, open a pile of files, run the full type-check and the full test suite.
The problem isn't wanting full coverage. The problem is doing it by **scanning**.

An index inverts that:

dsh-code-impact README · What you get：Two tools, registered into every agent session — plus a browsable page of the same index
(**Settings → Code Impact**).

dsh-code-impact README · `code_query`：| `op` | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `find` | where is this symbol (`addNode`, `Graph.addNode`, `ts:src/x.ts#Graph.addNode`) |
| `outline` | declaration skeleton of one file, with line ranges, exports, heritage clauses |
| `refs` | who mentions this symbol — each site resolved individually, so a same-named local doesn't count |
| `hierarchy` | extends / implements / subtypes / members (own, inherited, overridden) |
| `search` | substring match over names and signatures |
| `status` | index size, root, cache location, engine mode, parse failures |

dsh-code-impact README · `code_query`：```
find "parseTimeout" — 1 match

ts:src/config.ts#parseTimeout
  variable  src/config.ts:1-1  exported  refs:3

```
refs ts:src/config.ts#parseTimeout — 3 sites (exported, refs:3)
  variable src/config.ts:1  parseTimeout = 30 ;
  confidence: exact 3 · resolved 0 · heuristic 0 · unresolved mentions 0

dsh-code-impact README · `code_verify`：Call it after editing instead of re-scanning. It re-parses only the files that changed on disk
(and discovers new ones), then reports a symbol-level diff:

```
verify — verdict: internal
  1 file changed (0 deleted) · +0 -0 symbols · 1 body-only

body-only (signature unchanged, callers unaffected):

```
verify — verdict: breaking
  1 file changed (0 deleted) · +1 -1 symbols · 1 contract

symbols that no longer exist:

dsh-code-impact README · `code_verify`：`verdict` has four levels: `clean` (nothing changed), `internal` (implementation only),
`contract` (signature/export changed, callers may need edits), `breaking` (some reference no
longer resolves).

dsh-code-impact README · `code_verify`：A reference is only called dangling when it **used to resolve to the symbol that went away**. A
mention that never resolved in the first place — `filepath.Base`, a package that is not installed,
a name the heuristic merely guessed at — is not reported, because a false alarm costs more than a
missed one.

dsh-code-impact README · `code_verify`：The rule that makes it useful in practice: `const timeout = 30` → `= 60` is a **value change**,
reported as body-only, never as a contract change. Containers (class / interface / struct) are not
listed themselves — their members already express the change, so one memo edit doesn't drag the
whole class into the report.

dsh-code-impact README · `code_verify`：`code_verify` is **incremental**: it reports changes since the index last synced. Ask twice without
editing in between and the second answer is `clean`. That's the intended loop — one question after
each edit, and the answer is about what you just did.

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：The same index is browsable: **Settings → Code Impact**. Three views over the workspace, drawn from
the index rather than from a fresh scan:

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：| view | what it answers |
| --- | --- |
| Architecture | a treemap of directories weighted by symbol count, coloured by language — where the code actually lives |
| Imports | the file-level import graph as a chord diagram; hover a file to isolate its edges |
| Inheritance | the type hierarchy by depth, `implements` drawn dashed |
| Sessions | which sessions used the plugin, what they asked, what came back |

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：Clicking a file lists its symbols with kind, signature and line; clicking a type shows its
supertypes, subtypes and the file that declares it. The header carries the honesty chips —
files / symbols / names / languages, when the index was built, and a warning when files were
skipped — plus a `Refresh` button that re-checks the disk before redrawing.

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：The **Sessions** tab is the plugin's own audit trail: every `code_query` / `code_verify` call is
recorded per session (id, working directory, call counts, and the last 40 calls with their target
and one-line outcome). It is written to `$DSH_HOME/cache/code-index/usage.json`, so it survives a
restart and covers sessions this process never saw. It records the plugin's own calls only — it is
not an authority on what the agent did — and `Clear` empties it without touching the index.

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：`Open full page` puts the same map in a browser tab (`/code-impact/app`) with more room and no
settings chrome behind it; the two views share the same routes and the same index.

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：The page draws **one indexed workspace at a time**, and the folder box under the header is how a
second one gets in: type an absolute path (`D:\work\my-project`), press Enter, and the page builds
an index for it and switches to it. The same workspace stays in the dropdown afterwards. This is
the only way a workspace appears without the agent using a tool in it first — a session whose cwd
is the project also indexes it, implicitly, the first time `code_query` runs.

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：It is a client half of the bundle (`client.js`, React, theme tokens only — no iframe, no inline
HTML), talking to the host through read routes, one build route, and the usage routes. The
standalone page (`web/app.html` + `web/app.js`, plain DOM and SVG) is served from the same host:

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：```
GET  /code-impact/api/roots
GET  /code-impact/api/overview?root=<abs path>&refresh=1
GET  /code-impact/api/file?root=<abs path>&path=<repo-relative path>
POST /code-impact/api/index          {"root": "<absolute path>"}

dsh-code-impact README · The index page：Reads are allow-listed: the page can only read a directory that is already indexed, or the
session's working directory. `POST /index` is the one route that does work on request — it builds a
cache for the exact directory you named and nothing else, refuses relative paths, missing
directories and plain files with a `400` carrying the reason, and never writes inside your
repository.

dsh-code-impact README · Install：`dsh-code-impact` is a DSH host bundle: zero dependencies, plain ESM, one patch row.

```bash

dsh-code-impact README · from GitHub (or any published tarball / registry package)：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Locael123/dsh-code-impact
dsh web    # restart: the host half of a plugin is imported once, at boot
```

Manual install — only if the package is already resolvable from the profile's `node_modules`
(`plugin_manager` does that for you; a bare `cordis.yml` row alone will not):
yaml
- id: dsh-code-impact
  name: dsh-code-impact
  config:
    maxFiles: 20000
```

The bundle ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, so the plugin manager path is preferred — it wires the
patch row, links the directory, and keeps `files[]` correct.

dsh-code-impact README · from a local checkout：| config | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxFiles` | `20000` | cap on files per build; truncation is reported in `status` |
| `root` | session working directory | override the indexed root |

Cache: `$DSH_HOME/cache/code-index/<hash(root)>/` — content-addressed `facts/` plus a
`manifest.json`. Editing one file rewrites one fact. It is a **cache**: delete it any time, it
rebuilds; it is never written inside the indexed repo.

dsh-code-impact README · Precision contract：A file that fails to parse never disappears silently: `code_query op=status` reports
`warning: N file(s) could not be parsed and are NOT indexed`, and `code_verify` states it in
`unverified:`. If the index is under-counting, you get told.

When in doubt it returns candidates rather than "not found".

dsh-code-impact README · Scope & limits：- **Languages**: TypeScript / JavaScript / Go (`.ts .tsx .mts .cts .js .jsx .mjs .cjs .go`).
- **Module resolution**: relative paths with extension and `/index` probing, `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`
  `baseUrl` + `paths`, `go.mod` module prefix with same-package directories.
- **Skipped**: `node_modules` `.git` `dist` `build` `out` `vendor` `target` `__pycache__` `.venv`
  and friends, files over 512 KiB, binaries.
- **Deliberately approximate**: TS `implements` and Go interface satisfaction are structural /
  implicit, so they yield a candidate set marked `heuristic`. This is the only place the tool
  knowingly guesses.
- **Not modelled**: cross-language edges (a Go interface to its implementors, a JSON schema to its
  consumers), dynamic dispatch, generated code.

dsh-code-impact README · How it works：- **Facts, not graphs.** Each file stores only what *this* file says: `imports`, `exports`,
  `decls` (with heritage and members), `refs` (name + position + role + lexical scope). There is no
  target ID on disk. Name → definition is resolved **at query time**, which is why editing one file
  invalidates exactly one file.
- **Stable SymbolId**: `<lang>:<path>#<qualname>`, no line numbers. A rename or move changes the ID,
  and that change is itself the signal.
- **Freshness**: a query `stat`s the files in its answer before returning (`mtime` + `size`), so a
  stale hit is impossible for anything it reports. `code_verify` drives incremental re-indexing;
  external edits are caught by the same stat check; a structural change bumps a manifest version and
  rebuilds.
- **No native modules, no LSP, no subprocess.** A hand-written lexer plus a scope-aware resolver per
  language keeps cold start in the hundreds of milliseconds and the whole plugin dependency-free.

dsh-code-impact README · How it works：Measured on a 42-file mixed TS/Go workspace: cold build 276 ms, 883 symbols; queries 1–4 ms;
warm start from manifest 3 ms for a 5-file fixture.

dsh-code-impact README · Development：```bash
node test/selftest.mjs               # index + tools, 36 assertions
node test/addroot.mjs               # the page's "index a folder" path, including its refusals
node test/usage.mjs                 # the usage ledger: per-session records, persistence, clearing
node test/webcheck.mjs <repo>        # the JSON routes the page calls

dsh-code-impact README · Development：The self-test copies `test/fixture` — a deliberately small TS + Go project with a `tsconfig` path
alias, a class hierarchy, and a two-package Go module — into a temp directory, builds a real index,
and runs 36 assertions: body-only edits are not reported as contract changes, a renamed export
surfaces its dangling references, a renamed directory does not, new files are picked up, deleted
files are reported, Go cross-package references resolve `exact`, warm start reloads from the
manifest, and a file that mentions `constructor` still parses (that one was a real bug: a plain
object used as a delimiter stack hit `Object.prototype.constructor`).
